draft.title: Describing an association
card: Direction
Positive: as one variable increases, the other tends to increase. Negative: as one increases, the other tends to decrease. No direction: no clear trend.
Form
Linear if the points follow a straight line pattern. Non-linear if they follow a curve.
Strength
Strong if the points sit close to a clear pattern. Weak if they are widely scattered around it. Moderate sits in between.
A strong association does not prove that one variable causes the other. Both may be affected by a third variable, or the link may be coincidence.
draft.remember: Describe direction, form and strength. A strong association does not prove cause.

a.q: On a scatterplot, points slope downwards from left to right and sit close to a straight line. Which description fits best?
opts: Negative, linear and strong
Positive, linear and strong
Negative, linear and weak
Negative, non-linear and strong
a.why: Points sloping down show a negative direction. A straight line pattern is linear, and points close to the line make it strong. Positive is wrong because the other variable decreases as the first increases.
a.clue: Read the points from left to right: do they rise or fall?

b.q: In Geelong, daily ice cream sales and daily sunburn cases have a strong positive linear association. What can be concluded?
opts: It does not prove ice cream sales cause sunburn
Ice cream sales must cause the sunburn cases
Sunburn cases must cause the ice cream sales
The association is weak because there is no cause
b.why: A strong association does not prove cause. A third variable, such as hot sunny weather, may affect both. The cause option is tempting but strength only describes how close the points are to the pattern.
b.clue: Think about what else could affect both variables on a hot day.

b.best: It does not prove ice cream sales cause sunburn

problems.detail: Two distractors use "must" while the card says a third variable "may" affect both. The only hedged option stands out, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The card and question a are correct. In question b, the absolute "must" wording in two distractors makes the correct, hedged option easy to spot without understanding the idea.
